study.question: Does the committed task-private linear readout add incremental validation utility to the stronger pair-rank-occupancy source, exceeding both frozen source scores at justified measured cost?
study.hypothesis: The inspected pair source compresses history into one shared DIN sum for every task tower, despite its richer shared pair/feedback tokens. Task-conditioned signed item/action relevance and a separate projected first-rank summary can preserve useful task distinctions alongside that shared representation. This is a compatibility/utility hypothesis about the exact imported private-linear readout on the newer source, not proof of negative transfer or interference in the parent. Both sources share ancestry; their scores alone do not establish this mechanism.

nearest_work.difference: Preserve this complete stronger source and append the imported task-private readout. Its four towers currently receive the same pooled[:,0] history vector.

Reuse the exact scorer initialization, task pooling, linear-basis arithmetic and tower readout; substitute the newer pair-rank-occupancy source for its older memory-joint/collapsed source. Dedicated task rank helper is renamed to preserve every original pair helper unchanged.

inherited_components: All pair-rank-occupancy embeddings, local activation, temporal/relation/pair summaries and count/rank banks, feedback memory, joint attention block, masks, static inputs and four tower structures
Exact committed task trunk: (4*96+16)=400 ->64 with Dice; four 64->32 Dice->1 heads; zero final score outputs; shared bias-free112->112 zero-start extra projection
Original signed, unnormalized task pooling C_t=sum_i s_ti v_i and linear-rank moment M_t=sum_i r_i s_ti v_i, with FP32 accumulation and no learned signed denominator
Frozen host training/data/visibility/scoring contract; scratch training and original RNG stream
study.proposed_difference: Append only the imported private-linear residual history readout to the intact stronger pair source. Task t receives the original shared DIN sum plus C_t+P(M_t) in its existing112-wide history slot. Rich shared tokens are unchanged and no token, embedding, loss, feature, tower width or external data is added. Added modules start at zero function; constructor RNG forks preserve inherited initialization. This exact source substitution is the contribution being tested; it is not an external novelty claim.
predictions: Primary: full validation four-task macro AUC exceeds 0.831886841754755 (and therefore also 0.8310755947860231). Beating only the weaker source fails this transfer target. Ties follow the frozen Logloss/parameter/trial-ID rules, and all four task changes are reported without a new veto.

The added residual is initially zero, including empty histories; masked IDs, invalid task masks and current target action cannot affect it. After score outputs open, task readouts can differ and projected rank gradients can become active. These are implementation checks, not evidence of predictive mechanism.

If the proposed signal matters, exploratory gains should occur among nonempty histories; empty-history residual itself remains zero. Trained empty-history predictions can change indirectly through inherited parameters, so full trained-model equality on that slice is not predicted.

Static expected size is33177257 total =33130405+46852, with31793216 embedding and1384041 dense parameters; host measured training/inference cost must be reported. Lower cost or an equal-compute advantage is not predicted.
falsifiers: Candidate macro AUC <=0.831886841754755 weakens the claimed incremental transfer even if it exceeds the weaker source. A worse result is a failed implementation of this transfer, not a universal refutation of task-private modeling.

Invariance violations, nonfinite probabilities/gradients, a changed inherited initialization/data order, or dead task parameters after a nonzero diagnostic invalidate this implementation before an effectiveness conclusion.

A future active mean-routing or copy-basis matched control matching/exceeding the full candidate would weaken task-specific routing or rank attribution respectively; a source-by-readout factorial with no interaction would reject a stronger complementarity claim. These controls are not measured in this proposal.
An apparent single-seed improvement that disappears under paired repetitions would weaken robustness. No significance, mechanism, or repeated-support claim is allowed from the planned single run.
